Answer: B
Reason: The serial chest X-rays (dated 1999, 2000, and 2004) demonstrate a clear progression from initial nodular densities in the middle and lower lung fields to extensive, diffuse bilateral infiltrative disease with increasing radiolucencies (suggesting cavitation or necrosis), consistent with advanced bronchioloalveolar carcinoma. Options suggesting stability, regression, or isolated upper lobe involvement are contradicted by the visible worsening and distribution of opacities over time.
